competency_fulfillment.rationale: Every one of the 6 samples asks 'What is the weight of the object in g?' -- 'weight' is used where the competency's own noun is 'mass', and only the gram unit of the three named units (g, kg, mg) is ever exercised.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Across mcq seeds 42-46 and the cloze-formatted seed 50, the answer values are 15, 5, 53, 35, 10 and 64 grams -- six data points, zero of which are in kilograms or milligrams despite the competency naming all three units.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The stem 'What is the weight of the object in g?' is a single 8-word clause with no subordinate structure, comfortably within grade 3 quarter 2 reading demand across all 6 seeds including the cloze variant at seed 50.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The competency requires measuring 'using appropriate measuring tools', but none of the 6 rendered stems names or references a scale, balance, or any specific tool -- the reading device stays entirely implicit behind the phrase 'the object'.

competency_alignment.rationale: The competency's stated noun is 'mass', yet the rendered vocabulary in all 6 samples is 'weight' ('What is the weight of the object in g?'), a term this node's competency text never uses, so the observed wording drifts from the exact vocabulary being taught.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The sampled gram values (5, 10, 15, 35, 53, 64 across seeds 42-46 and 50) are sensible small-object readings for an introductory grams-only presentation, appropriate in magnitude for what is actually shown.
